defects.description: The 1% with an alcohol use disorder is described as 'about one in ten', but 1% is one in a hundred, not one in ten.
paraphrases: 1% is one in a hundred, so 'one in ten' is wrong.
One in ten would be 10%, not 1%.
The percentage (1%) and the fraction (one in ten) disagree.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'one in a hundred' (1%). Findable from the percentage and fraction in the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: If more than half of traffic deaths are attributable to alcohol, then fewer than half come from other causes, but the text says 'more than half from all other causes'.
defects.anchor: more than half from all other
paraphrases: More than half from alcohol leaves fewer than half from other causes, not more than half.
Two 'more than half' shares would exceed the whole.
The alcohol and non-alcohol shares of traffic deaths cannot both exceed half.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'fewer than half' (complement of more than half). Findable within the sentence, distinct.

paraphrases: 22.1 litres / 365 days is about 60 mL/day, not 600.
The daily figure is roughly ten times too high.
22,100 mL over a year is around 60 mL per day.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'roughly 60 millilitres' (22.1 L / 365). Findable from the annual figure, distinct.
